_**Search for the Gods**_ is a 1975 [made-for-television][drama] "Drama (film and television)") film directed by [Jud Taylor]. It stars [Kurt Russell] and [Stephen McHattie].[[1]] It was intended to be the [pilot episode] of a TV series that never made it into production.

## Plot

[[edit]]

Three young adventurers—Willie Longfellow, Genera Juantez, and Shan Mullins—are searching for parts of a mysterious golden tablet, which brings to light evidence that [astronauts] from another world visited Earth in ancient times and had a profound effect on the technological advancement of the human race.

## Cast

[[edit]]

* [Kurt Russell] as Shan Mullins
* [Stephen McHattie] as Willie Longfellow
* [Ralph Bellamy] as Dr. Henderson
* Victoria Racimo as Genera Juantez
* [Raymond St. Jacques] as Raymond Stryker
* [Albert Paulsen] as Tarkanian
* [John War Eagle] as Lucio
* [Carmen Argenziano] as Wheeler

**Stephen McHattie Smith** (born February 3, 1947)[[1]][[2]] is a Canadian actor.[[3]] Since beginning his professional career in 1970, he has amassed over 200 film, television, and theatre credits; and has collaborated with directors like [Darren Aronofsky], [Bruce McDonald] "Bruce McDonald (director)"), and [David Cronenberg]. He played Jimmy Murray on the [CBC] drama _[Emily of New Moon] "Emily of New Moon (TV series)")_ (1998-2000) and Sgt. Frank Coscarella on the police procedural _[Cold Squad]_ (1999-2001).

He won the [Genie Award for Best Supporting Actor] for his performance as [Dick Irvin] in _[The Rocket] "The Rocket (2005 film)")_, and was nominated for [Best Actor] for [_Pontypool_] "Pontypool (film)"). He was nominated for a [Drama Desk Award] for [Yehoshua Sobol]'s [_Ghetto_] "Ghetto (play)") and won an [Obie Award] for _Mensch Meier_.

## Early life

[[edit]]

McHattie was born in [Antigonish, Nova Scotia], on February 3, 1947 (the year of his birth has also been cited as 1945, 1946, and 1948), and raised in [Guysborough County].[[1]] At 16, he began acting in local amateur plays and at 19 moved to [New York City], where he studied at the [American Academy of Dramatic Arts].[[1]][[4]]

## Career

[[edit]]

McHattie began his career on stage in the 1968 Broadway production of [_The American Dream_] "The American Dream (play)"). Two years later he made his film debut in [_The People Next Door_] "The People Next Door (1970 film)"). He appeared in other Broadway plays, including _[Mourning Becomes Electra]_ in 1972, _[The Iceman Cometh]_ in 1973, and [_Ghetto_] "Ghetto (play)") in 1989, for which he was nominated for a [Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Actor in a Play].[[5]]

McHattie has appeared in many films and television shows including _[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]_, _[Star Trek: Enterprise]_, _[Highlander: The Series]_, and [American Playhouse]'s _[Life Under Water]_ (1989). His roles include _[300] "300 (film)")_, _[A History of Violence] "A History of Violence (film)")_, _[The Fountain] "The Fountain (film)")_, _[Secretary] "Secretary (2002 film)")_, _[Shoot 'Em Up] "Shoot 'Em Up (film)")_, _[Life with Billy] "Life with Billy (film)")_, _[One Dead Indian]_, _[Beverly Hills Cop III]_. In Canada, he appeared in _[Canada: A People's History]_ as Canadian hero Major-General Sir [Isaac Brock], and in _[The Rocket] "The Rocket (2005 film)")_ as coach [Dick Irvin].[[6]]

He portrayed an extraordinary [USMC] sniper (based on real life sniper [Carlos Hathcock]) in the _[JAG] "JAG (TV series)")_ season one episode "High Ground". In 1976, he played iconic American actor [James Dean] in the television movie _[James Dean] "James Dean (1976 film)")_, a television adaptation of the biography written by James Dean's friend and writer [Bill Bast].[[6]] McHattie appeared in several mini-series, including _[Centennial] "Centennial (miniseries)")_ and _Roughnecks_.[[6]]

McHattie appeared in several episodes of _[Seinfeld]_ (beginning with "[The Pitch] "The Pitch (Seinfeld)")") as Dr. Reston, [Elaine Benes]'s manipulative [psychiatrist] boyfriend; he also appeared in two episodes of _[The X-Files]_. From 1998 to 2000, he had a recurring role in the Canadian-made TV series _[Emily of New Moon] "Emily of New Moon (TV series)")_, based upon the 1923 novel by [Lucy Maud Montgomery]. From 1999-2001, he portrayed Sgt. Frank Coscarella in the Canadian police procedural drama, _[Cold Squad]_. Since 2005, he has appeared as Captain Healy, Massachusetts State Police Homicide Division Commander, in the first eight of the _[Jesse Stone]#Television\_adaptations "Jesse Stone (character)")_ series TV movies, which are based on the novels of [Robert B. Parker]. He did not appear in the ninth instalment however.[[6]] He appeared in the pilot of _[Sabbatical]?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sabbatical (TV series) (page does not exist)")_, voiced the villain [The Shade] in _[Justice League] "Justice League (TV series)")_, and portrayed Hollis Mason, the first [Nite Owl], in the film adaptation of _[Watchmen] "Watchmen (2009 film)")_.[[7]]

McHattie had a well-received[[8]] appearance in the sixth season episode "[In the Pale Moonlight]" of _[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]_, as [Romulan] Senator Vreenak, who is the target of a Federation [false flag] operation to deceive the Romulan Empire into declaring war on the [Dominion] "Dominion (Star Trek)"). The episode has often been cited as one of the best episodes of _Star Trek_ ever produced,[[9]][[10]][[11]] and McHattie’s reading of the line “It’s a fake!” has been ranked amongst the greatest moments in _Star Trek_[[12]] and spawned an online meme.[[13]]

In 2009, McHattie appeared in the Canadian IFC film _[Pontypool] "Pontypool (film)")_ and in the Canadian thriller _[Summer's Blood]_ as Gant Hoxey, alongside _[Twilight] "The Twilight Saga (film series)")_ actress [Ashley Greene], who portrays Summer. He co-starred with [Felicia Day] and [Kavan Smith] in the Gothic adaptation of [Red Riding Hood], _[Red: Werewolf Hunter]_.[[14]] In 2015, he appeared in the supernatural thriller _[Pay the Ghost]_.[[6]]

## Personal life

[[edit]]

McHattie is married to actress Lisa Houle, with whom he has three children. He was previously married to actress [Meg Foster].[[6]] His older brother is actor [Wendell Smith] "Wendell Smith (actor)").[[15]]

**Kurt Vogel Russell** (born March 17, 1951) is an American actor. He began his career as a child actor before transitioning to leading roles as an adult in various genres such as [action adventures], science-fiction, [westerns], [romance films], [comedic films], and [family dramas]. He is known for collaborating with filmmakers such as [John Carpenter] and [Quentin Tarantino], and has received a [Critics' Choice Super Award] as well as various award nominations, including for a [Primetime Emmy Award] and a [Golden Globe Award].

At the age of 12, he began acting in the [Western TV series]_[The Travels of Jaimie McPheeters] "The Travels of Jaimie McPheeters (TV series)")_ (1963–1964). In the late 1960s, he signed a ten-year contract with [Walt Disney Productions], starring in films such as _[The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes]_ (1969), _[Now You See Him, Now You Don't]_ (1972), and _[The Strongest Man in the World]_ (1975). For his portrayal of [rock and roll][superstar][Elvis Presley] in the television film _[Elvis] "Elvis (1979 film)")_ (1979), he was nominated for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited Series or Movie].[[1]]

Russell was nominated for a [Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture] for his role in [Mike Nichols]'s _[Silkwood]_ (1983). He collaborated with director [John Carpenter] playing [antiheroes] in the action films _[Escape from New York]_ (1981) and its sequel _[Escape from L.A.]_ (1996), the horror film _[The Thing] "The Thing (1982 film)")_ (1982), and the comedy action film _[Big Trouble in Little China]_ (1986). Russell also acted in _[Used Cars]_ (1980), _[The Fox and the Hound]_ (1981), _[The Best of Times] "The Best of Times (1986 film)")_ (1986), _[Overboard] "Overboard (1987 film)")_ (1987), _[Backdraft] "Backdraft (film)")_ (1991), [Captain Ron] (1992), _[Tombstone] "Tombstone (film)")_ (1993), _[Stargate] "Stargate (film)")_ (1994), _[Vanilla Sky]_ (2001), _[Miracle] "Miracle (2004 film)")_ (2004), _[Dreamer] "Dreamer (2005 film)")_, _[Sky High] "Sky High (2005 film)")_ (both 2005), _[Death Proof]_ (2007), _[The Hateful Eight]_ (2015), _[Bone Tomahawk]_ (2015), and _[Once Upon a Time in Hollywood]_ (2019).

Russell has also acted in several franchises, portraying Mr. Nobody in three films of the _[Fast & Furious]_ franchise from 2015 to 2021, [Ego] in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe] (MCU) installments _[Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2]_ (2017) and _[What If...?] "What If...? (TV series)")_ (2021), and [Santa Claus] in the [Netflix] films _[The Christmas Chronicles]_ (2018) and _[The Christmas Chronicles 2]_ (2020).[[2]][[3]]

## Early life

[[edit] | [edit source]]

Kurt Vogel Russell was born on March 17, 1951,[[4]] at [Wesson Maternity Hospital] in [Springfield, Massachusetts].[[5]] His father, [Bing Russell], was also an actor. His mother, Louise Julia (née Crone) Russell,[[6]] was a dancer.[[7]] Russell has three sisters,[[7]] Jill Franco,[[8]] Jamie and Jody.[[7]] His family relocated to California when he was a child, and Russell grew up in [Thousand Oaks].[[9]] Russell played little league baseball throughout his grade school years[[10]][[11]] and also on his high school baseball team as a second baseman.[[12]] He graduated from [Thousand Oaks High School] in California in 1969.[[13]] He signed a minor league contract in 1971 and played two seasons in the Class A Northwest League where he was an all-star infielder. He suffered a career-ending shoulder surgery in 1973 at Class AA El Paso.[[14]] His father also played professional baseball in the minor leagues. His older sister, Jill, is the mother of former professional baseball player [Matt Franco].[[15]] From 1969 to 1975, Russell served in the [California Air National Guard] and belonged to the [146th Tactical Airlift Wing], then based in [Van Nuys].[[16]]
